name: Tryout
why: Borrowing a shop member's On Recruit without buying it is a clean twist on the shop and pays off whatever is face up.

name: Gather
why: Word-for-word the same as Stash and Allowance; fine fuel with a recruit rider but adds no red angle.

name: Walk-In
why: Blind recruit from the pile with a gift to every rival; you don't know what you pay for until it flips.

name: Promote
why: Trading up into a rival's better member is a real table moment and feeds Foster Parents and Deprogrammers; give/recruit wording needs a read.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote; trading down for 3 red is mostly a resource play that gifts the rival a better card.

name: Initiation
why: A free recruit up to 8 in round III is a plain, big burst any trailing player can grab.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Every Round Start swap with a rival makes the table watch its members; Loyalists is the visible answer.

name: Volunteer
why: Cheap filler that only exists to trigger recruit effects; nobody notices it.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two recruits for one buy and 3 red-member count; simple and satisfying, pricey.

name: Proselytizers
why: +1 follower per recruit is the red engine piece; stacks with Gather, Initiation and free recruits.

name: Mob
why: Rewards the red contest leader again each round; 12 cost makes it hard to move and pure rich-get-richer.

name: Recruiter
why: +1 red per recruit at cost 6 is a small trickle nobody feels.

name: Patriarch
why: Game-end payoff for a wide cult; fits red quantity but quiet.

name: Foster Parents
why: Cheap, fires off Promote, Demote, Body Snatchers and Poach; makes member movement pay.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Counts as 4 red members for 3 cost is a contest swing; the follower sting rides on member steals.

name: Panel
why: Self-promote or demote is a smart upgrade, but 'promote or demote another of your members' needs the space rules looked up.

name: Loyalists
why: Plain defense against swaps that counts 3 for the contest; rivals see it and re-aim.

name: Clerk
why: Flat +1 red each round for 5 cost: forgettable and dead.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple plus the Goes Last token ties straight into the went-last contest; a clear hold-or-take call.

name: Hold Up
why: Skipping whoever is next, even yourself, is a short rule that bends the snake; the self-skip makes timing a real choice.

name: Right Away
why: A small take-two-in-a-row that sets up Courier; fine but modest.

name: Last Call
why: Pays for holding minions back and grabs the last spot; strong but wordy.

name: Crunch Time
why: Two turns right away in few words reshapes the snake; great burst for whoever needs it.

name: Overtime
why: Round III extra minion is a nice bump but works the same for anyone and repeats Extra Hand.

name: Courier
why: Consecutive turns paying one of each color links purple timing to yellow sets; builds with Right Away and Crunch Time.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays when a rival takes Goes Last, but 'per minion on it' is unclear about what is counted.

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion after your last from round II is powerful; 8 cost makes it hard to answer.

name: Early Birds
why: Cheap immunity to skips; a clean counter to Hold Up and Bouncers.

name: Bouncers
why: Skipping the next two rivals on recruit is a big, timed moment; Early Birds blocks it.

name: Gossip
why: Pays on any skip at the table; stacks with Hold Up and Bouncers.

name: Timekeeper
why: Same 'per member of my color' game-end shape as Snobs and Old Money; nothing purple about it.

name: Closer
why: Rewards the same last minion the contest already counts; neat but a small bonus.

name: Hot Streak
why: Big payoff for chains, but counting the turns in a row just before this one has to be remembered.

name: Picket Line
why: Cheap 3-count member that taxes rivals on purple spaces; rivals notice.

name: Bell Ringer
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do: whether the Goes Last token was placed before a skip and which turns came in a row
why: Unreadable condition chain for +1 purple; nobody can say when it fires.

name: Toast
why: Big silver with gifts to everyone; feeds rivals' silver contest, clear but blunt.

name: Polish
why: A plain 2-for-4 converter; yellow-ish work, quiet.

name: Party Gifts
why: Followers for handing rivals contest silver is a real tension in few words.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pay one then gain two; everyone touches it but the trade is muddy.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver plus conversion, already what Polish does; quiet.

name: Largesse
why: Up to 10 followers for handing rivals the round III silver contest; a big how-much call.

name: Godparent
why: Giving away a member for its cost in followers is a big swing and combos with Old Maid and Foster Parents.

name: Hostesses
why: Steady gifts and followers each round; everyone gets a little, fine.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver on any gift, the whole table's; small trigger.

name: Guest of Honor
why: +4 for gifting a cheap member each Silver space; makes giving members a plan and pairs with Old Maid.

name: Toastmaster
why: +1 follower per Silver space: forgettable.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling silver once is a big timed moment that also tips rivals 2 each.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as any color is a strong rule bend at 11 cost, overlapping Alchemists.

name: Philanthropist
why: A smaller Party Gifts on a member; repeats its sibling space.

name: Creditor
why: Taking 2 followers each round from a chosen rival who gets paid in silver; aimable at the leader.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Once-per-game silver collection from everyone; fine timing call.

name: High Society
why: Pays when rivals take Silver spaces; same shape as Picket Line.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (target picked by comparing rivals' resources)
why: Gains by comparing your silver to the richest rival's; the rival-resources shape.

name: Harvest
why: The plain fuel space with color choice; anchors sets.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads where rivals sit to pick a color; interactive but takes a count.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards recruiting a new color, good yellow tie, wordy round table.

name: Housewarming
why: Free new-color recruit up to 5 pushes variety cleanly.

name: Melting Pot
why: Scales with your color spread; simple yellow payoff.

name: Makeover
why: Round III rearrange fixes sets and contests; quiet but useful.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills missing colors toward sets; cheap catch-up that scales with what you lack.

name: Duty Collector
why: Pays when rivals recruit your colors; small and needs attention.

name: Tourist
why: Followers per color held every round; a strong steady engine.

name: Seamstress
why: Doubling full sets is a big timed moment, but what 'double' gives needs asking.

name: Dyer
why: Same per-color-held shape as Tourist and Caravan, paid in yellow.

name: Meddler
why: Breaks rivals' sets one resource each; small jab, fiddly.

name: Drifters
why: Pick a color to count as; links into red's contest, New Blood and Big Tent.

name: Big Tent
why: Game-end bonus for one of each color shapes every recruit.

name: Caravan
why: One of each held color every round at 9 cost; snowballs for the wide leader.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
why: Yellow as a wild in sets; tidy yellow rule bend.

name: Savings
why: Blue fuel plus a shop-cycling rider; fine.

name: Out of Style
why: Clears a color from the shop; denies rivals' targets in one line.

name: Peek
why: Setting up the pile is a smart blue move, though the order must be remembered.

name: Recruit Twice
why: An extra buy is the most valuable thing late; plain and strong.

name: Bury
why: Hate-drafting a shop member for half its cost; clear interaction.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in round III is a burst any trailer can grab.

name: Hawker
why: Offering a shop member round the table is a real auction moment, but wordy.

name: Patroness
why: Pays on any bottom-of-pile event, the whole blue toolkit's; connects many cards.

name: Snobs
why: Per blue member at game end; repeats Timekeeper and Old Money.

name: Window Shopper
why: Cycles the shop and pays colors; steady blue churn.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn bends the core rule; at 9 cost it runs away for whoever lands it.

name: Window Dressers
why: Cheap 3-count member that wipes the shop once; overlaps Out of Style.

name: Doormen
why: Swapping a rival's member for a shop one each round is a strong sting; replacement rule needs a read.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue on follower buys has nothing to do with the shop.

name: Trendsetters
why: Each recruit cycles the shop; fine, overlaps Window Shopper.

name: Critic
why: +1 follower when rivals recruit blue; small.

name: Scavenger
hardFail: turn flow: asks its owner to choose and recruit during a rival's turn
why: Strong link to every bury card in the game, but the owner acts on a rival's turn.

name: Help Yourself
why: Scaling aimed theft; the core magenta check on hoards.

name: Stash
why: Identical to Gather and Allowance; no magenta angle.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a round of safety; clean defensive pick.

name: Heist
why: Steal 3 followers: plain and aimable at the leader.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim chooses their own punishment; feels bad.

name: Poach
why: Round III outright member take; big and clear.

name: Cutpurse
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (target picked by comparing rivals' resources)
why: Targets the rival with the most resources.

name: Accomplice
why: Cheap steal 3 on recruit; plain and punchy.

name: Grifter
why: Steal scales with cult size; rewards the wide leader.

name: Second-Story Man
why: Steal 2 before contests: swings a contest and can be aimed at a leader.

name: Desperado
why: Bigger steals while last; real catch-up, condition needs checking.

name: Extortionist
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (target picked by comparing rivals' resources)
why: Targets the rival with the most resources twice a round.

name: Bodyguards
why: Full steal immunity; clean but switches off a whole kind of answer.

name: Double Agent
why: Swap with a rival on recruit; whether it then fires for them is unclear.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a member from the widest rival every round; the victim loses members early with no say.

name: Shoplifter
why: Steal 1 per recruit; small engine piece.

name: Fence
why: Pays when robbed; a neat answer to theft.

name: Allowance
why: Identical to Gather and Stash; no white angle.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for spending on a recruit; scale changes by round.

name: Exchange
why: A better follower buy; competes with the core buy rather than bending it.

name: Farewell
why: Cashing out a member for its cost combos with Martyrs and Old Maid.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell paid in white; repeats its sibling.

name: Cash In
why: All white to followers in round III; the payoff white builds toward.

name: Recluse
why: Rewards a small cult against wide rivals; real catch-up.

name: Landlord
why: Flat +2 white; nothing but a flat one-color gain.

name: Heiresses
why: Once-per-game white per member feeds Cash In; a timed combo.

name: Brokers
why: +1 on every White follower payout; steady engine piece.

name: Misers
why: Holding white for game end against Cash In is a real choice.

name: Raiders
why: Steal 4 followers once, paying 2 white; aimable at the leader.

name: Cashier
why: Cash In on a member; repeats the round III space.

name: Money Changers
why: Pays on anyone's follower buys; constant small trickle.

name: Martyrs
why: Pays its cost when it leaves; combos with Farewell, Promote, Godparent, Poach.

name: Old Money
why: Per white member at game end; repeats Snobs and Timekeeper.

name: Hoarder
why: Turn everything white once; sets up Cash In and Misers.

name: Build Up
why: The plain fuel anchor for green.

name: Echo
why: Copy the previous action: tiny text, deep because of whatever just happened.

name: Reprise
why: Copy your own earlier action; clean but self-contained.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival's On Recruit; reading their cult pays.

name: Cover
why: Copy an empty action; dodges blocking cleanly.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Every On Recruit again in round III; pays off a built cult.

name: Song Request
why: An extra rival-action copy every round; strong and reads the board.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrowing a rival's ability is fun, but which one it has must be remembered.

name: Impressionist
why: Pays on any copy at the table; small.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubles copy gains at 10 cost; snowballs for the green leader.

name: Fan Club
why: Copy the leader's action on recruit; catch-up built in.

name: Roadie
why: Per green member income; generic shape, no copying.

name: Stunt Double
why: Do the action you just took again; simple double and great timing.

name: Tribute Band
why: Do all of a rival's actions once: a huge moment at 14 cost.

name: Doppelganger
why: Becomes a copy of your best member; neat, needs a marker.

name: Agents
why: Blocks copying of your actions; a pure counter.

name: Encore
why: Next On Recruit twice; a timing combo that must be remembered.

name: Party Crasher
why: Placing on a taken space bends the blocking core once.

name: Alchemists
why: Everything as any when recruiting at 5 cost and worth 3; overlaps Smooth Talkers.

name: Extra Hand
why: +1 minion once for 9; same as Overtime, pricey.

name: Line Cutters
why: First every round for 2 cost and worth 3: must-buy that undoes catch-up turn order.

name: Old Maid
why: A hot potato: dump it with Promote, Demote, Godparent or Guest of Honor.

name: Dabblers
why: Counts as 2 wild members; 'wild' needs a lookup.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members each round; chaotic and powerful, hard to read.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancel a contest you can't win; real denial aimed at a leader.

name: Con Men
why: Steal 5 on recruit; a bigger Accomplice.

name: Sore Loser
why: Steals 5 from the top contest winner if you won none; ties unclear.
